```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev.args = list(bg = "white"), collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5
)
has_sf <- requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)
has_gg <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
has_td <- requireNamespace("tidydiversity", quietly = TRUE)
```

tidymapr is the mapping companion to
[tidydiversity](https://github.com/jmozez/tidydiversity). Every verb takes a
data frame and returns a tibble, an `sf` table, a `SpatRaster` or a ggplot,
so diversity estimates and maps stay in one tidy workflow, in the same way
dplyr and ggplot2 work together.

```{r setup}
library(tidymapr)
```

## Study sites

`geo_example_sites()` returns the published bait GPS of the Mt Wilhelm
ant survey behind `tidydiversity::png_ants` (`png_ants_sites`; Mottl,
Moses and Klimes 2023,
[doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8191946)),
one point per elevation band.

```{r sites}
sites <- geo_example_sites("wilhelm")
sites
```

`plot_sites()` draws a publication-ready study-site map with a scale bar
and north arrow.

```{r plot-sites, eval = has_sf && has_gg, fig.height = 5}
plot_sites(sites, lon, lat, colour = elevation_band, label = site)
```

## Sites as `sf` and distances

```{r sf, eval = has_sf}
geo_as_sf(sites, lon, lat)
```

```{r distance}
head(geo_distance(sites, lon, lat, site = site))
```

## Diversity on a map with tidydiversity

Load both packages and pipe diversity estimates straight onto a map.

```{r diversity-map, eval = has_sf && has_gg && has_td}
library(tidydiversity)
est <- div_estimate(png_ants, q = 0, nboot = 0, .by = season)
est <- dplyr::left_join(est, sites[c("site", "lon", "lat")], by = "site")
plot_geo(est[est$season == "dry", ], estimate, lon, lat, label = site)
```

`geo_decay()` joins geographic, elevational or environmental distances to
`tidydiversity::beta_pair()` so `tidydiversity::beta_decay_model()` can fit
distance-decay models.

See the article "Geospatial diversity workflows" for rasters, occurrence
cleaning, basemaps, bioclim layers, stem maps, spatial eigenvectors and
species distribution models.
